defs: Predict context words from the centre word.
Predict the centre word from averaged context vectors.
v (centre) and u (context): two vectors per word.
Normalising over all V words per pair is too costly.
Classify real (w, c) pairs vs K sampled noise pairs.
Counts Xᵢⱼ of word j in context of word i.
Weighted least squares fitting vᵢ·uⱼ + bᵢ + b̃ⱼ to log Xᵢⱼ.
formulas: P(c\mid w)=\frac{e^{\mathbf u_c^\top\mathbf v_w}}{\sum_k e^{\mathbf u_k^\top\mathbf v_w}}
J=\sum f(X_{ij})(\mathbf v_i^\top\mathbf u_j+b_i+\tilde b_j-\log X_{ij})^2
confused: Normalise over V vs 1 + K binary decisions.
Local windows, prediction vs global counts, regression.
Drop frequent training words vs choose negatives.
recall.minute: One-hot vectors are orthogonal (dot product 0) and long; Word2Vec learns dense vectors where relations are directions (king − man + woman ≈ queen). Skip-gram turns each centre word and its window neighbours into training pairs and models P(c|w) with a softmax over two vector sets, but the denominator over V (e.g. 100,000) words is a bottleneck. SGNS instead classifies real vs fake pairs: L = −log σ(v·u⁺) − Σ log σ(−v·u⁻), with K negatives from counts^0.75 and subsampling of frequent words (discard 1 − √(t/f), t ≈ 10⁻⁵). Gradients pull real contexts together and push negatives apart. Worked: v = [0.1, 0.3], u⁺ = [0.2, 0.9], u⁻ = [0.7, 0.1], α = 0.1: scores 0.29/0.10, σ ≈ 0.57/0.52, v → [0.0722, 0.3335], u⁺ → [0.2043, 0.9129], u⁻ → [0.6948, 0.0844]. CBOW averages contexts to predict the centre. GloVe builds global counts (I like cats/dogs/love: P(like|I) = 2/3), motivated by ratios such as P(solid|ice)/P(solid|steam) ≈ 8.9, and minimises Σ f(X)(v·u + b + b̃ − log X)² with f = (x/100)^0.75; worked J = 4.49 and v → [0.51896, 0.37064].
